item.title: From Prompt to Pwn: Cline Bot AI Coding Agent Vulnerabilities
item.description:
Author: Aaron Portnoy
Date: December 09, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Prompt Injection", "Software Vulnerabilities", "Machine Learning", "Cybersecurity"]
Summary:
  • AI coding assistants can be exploited via prompt injections.
  • Cline Bot AI has vulnerabilities including API key theft and code execution.
  • Exploits need only opening a malicious repo for analysis.
  • System prompts contain sensitive operational logic.
  • Disclosure of prompts increases attacker capabilities.
  • Security risks stem from prompt design and stored sensitive data.

item.title: Inside OpenAI Sora 2: Uncovering System Prompts Driving Multi-Modal LLMs
item.description:
Author: Aaron Portnoy
Date: December 09, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Large Language Models", "Multi-modal Models", "Prompt Engineering", "AI Security"]
Summary:
  • We revealed Sora 2's system prompt using multi-modal experiments.
  • Data transformations can cause errors and meaning shifts.
  • Multi-modal models increase semantic drift risks.
  • Prompt extraction helps understand model behavior.
  • Models resist prompt disclosure but can be circumvented.
  • This affects AI security and research.

item.title: Can a 14B Model Match a 100B+ Model? We Fine-Tuned 8+ Models to Find Out
item.description:
Author: Bauke Brenninkmeijer
Date: December 05, 2025
Tags: ["Machine Learning", "Natural Language Processing", "Model Fine-Tuning", "Text Classification"]
Summary:
  • We fine-tuned over 8 language models for text classification.
  • A 14B model outperformed 100B+ base models with 93.
  • 4% accuracy.
  • Prompt engineering improved accuracy by 34%.
  • Using LLM labeling cost $26 for 8,000 labels.
  • Smaller models can match much larger ones when well-tuned.
